note: Adapted from the original English description published with this species by Bacchus (1997); both the soldier and the large worker are described in prose, with measurement tables; the alate is given in the original as IMAGO. Unknown. The author notes that the soldier mandibles of this species are the longest in Microtermes (0.65—0.75 mm, versus 0.50—0.61 mm in other species). Several numbers in the OCR measurement table are misplaced (such as the row for head length including mandibles), and that row is not cited.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and labrum yellow to orange; mandibles brown with yellow bases; antennae, body and legs pale yellow; postmentum concolorous with the head, slightly darker than the genae. Head capsule elongate-rectangular, setae sparse, sides parallel or converging anteriorly and posteriorly, posterior margin evenly rounded; labrum short, extending to about the middle of the mandibles, broadly ligulate, apex rounded, with 5—8 setae on the anterior third; mandibles long, apex strongly upturned, inner margin finely serrate, curvature 0.08—0.10 mm; left mandible with a small tooth on the inner margin; antennae 14-segmented, segments 3 and 4 similar, segments 1 and 2 subequal. Postmentum very long and narrow. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin with a blunt angular notch in the middle, posterior margin slightly concave. Fore tibia moderately inflated; spurs 3, the dorsal spur about as long as the outer ventral spur; the single seta on the fore coxa not spine-like.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large worker: head capsule yellow to yellowish brown, postclypeal pad reddish brown; mandibles brown with pale yellow bases. Head capsule subrectangular, sides converging posteriorly, posterior margin broadly rounded; head setae regularly and symmetrically arranged; cranial suture forked; postclypeus inflated, thin-bean-shaped, median suture moderately distinct; anteclypeus flat, projecting forwards in the middle; antennae 14-segmented, segment 4 shortest, segments 3 and 5 similar, segments 1 and 2 subequal; labrum with a transverse sclerotic band, apex broadly rounded. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin shallowly concave in the middle, posterior margin straight, corners slightly rounded. Fore tibia not inflated; spurs 3, the dorsal spur about half the ventral outer spur; fore coxa conical, the large anterior seta not spine-like.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Soldier measurements (15 heads, 13 colonies, mm): head length to mandible base 1.00—1.23, maximum head width 0.75—0.85, head width behind antennal sockets 0.75—0.85, labrum length 0.28—0.33, width 0.25—0.28, left mandible transverse length 0.65—0.75, width 0.08—0.10, curvature 0.08—0.10, fore tibia length 0.58—0.65, width 0.13—0.15, hind tibia length 0.63—0.73, width 0.10—0.13, maximum pronotum width 0.50—0.63, postmentum length 0.63—0.85, maximum width 0.33—0.35. Large-worker measurements (10 heads, 6 colonies): head length to anterior margin of postclypeus 0.98—1.13, maximum head width 0.85—0.95, postclypeal pad length 0.18—0.23, width 0.35—0.39, maximum pronotum width 0.45—0.53, fore tibia length 0.50—0.55, hind tibia length 0.60—0.68. Holotype soldier collected at Lokori, Kenya; nests found in and beneath dead wood and dead tree stumps, mostly in Acacia tortilis thickets. Alate unknown.
